text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- Planned reform of the health system could lead to some hospitals becoming insolvent.

- Martin Kohlhaussen, chief executive of Germany's Commerzbank, said in Washington the bank may consider raising its stake in the Austro-Italian-German consortium to take over Creditanstalt if necessary. Kohlhaussen said he would welcome the return of Die Erste savings bank into the consortium.

- Austria is still behind in its privatisation of state firms compared to the 16 other OECD countries, a study says. A combination of strategic share holders and private investors is needed for a more effective privatisation programme.
- Before Austria becomes a member of NATO, an environmental and social union in Europe must be agreed upon, Chancellor Franz Vranitzky said at a rally for the European Parliament elections.
- Some 20,000 people watched Vienna's first snowboard event in the city.
- Germany reportedly does not trust Austria to put up the necessary border police for Austria's entry to Schengen by July 1997.
- Siemens Oesterreich has received an order for 132 million schillings from the Slovenian railways to renew their communications network.
- President Thomas Klestil should be ready to take up his duties soon, doctors said.
- A major U.S. bank, possibly Bank of America or Citibank, is rumoured as a possible bidder for the government's stake in Creditanstalt.
- Austria's economy is not competitive enough, research institute IHS said. Main problems cited were export deficits and the fact new markets were not being used to full potential.
